entries.title: BioShock

emulation.notes: Use native Windows. Console emulation is unnecessary for the researched route.

primary.why: BioShock originally shipped on Windows and Xbox 360, then PlayStation 3, Mac OS X, iOS, and later remastered platforms through BioShock: The Collection. The Windows BioShock Remastered route is the best complete archive route because the remaster targets higher resolution/framerate presentation, includes the formerly PlayStation 3-exclusive Challenge Rooms, and the collection includes all single-player DLC.
primary.how_to_play: Use BioShock Remastered on Windows from the current Steam/2K route for the main run. Keep the original Windows release as a fallback if remaster stability, audio, or launcher behavior becomes a capture issue.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PC release; useful fallback for original presentation and compatibility comparison.
all_releases.reason: skip: the remaster is the primary complete route, but the original Windows build remains the fallback if remaster issues interfere with capture.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console release.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower fidelity than the Windows remaster and no sourced exclusive single-player content over the remastered route.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PlayStation release that introduced Challenge Rooms content.
all_releases.reason: skip: the formerly PlayStation 3-exclusive Challenge Rooms are documented in BioShock Remastered, so this is not needed as a secondary route.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Mac port.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced exclusive content over the Windows remaster.

all_releases.fidelity: Mobile port of the original game.
all_releases.reason: skip: delisted/mobile route is not a fidelity or completeness win over Windows Remastered.

all_releases.fidelity: Remastered PC route with higher-resolution presentation and the strongest capture/settings ceiling.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity complete route with formerly PlayStation 3-exclusive Challenge Rooms included.

all_releases.fidelity: Remastered console route through BioShock: The Collection.
all_releases.reason: skip: strong console option, but Windows has the better capture/settings ceiling.

all_releases.fidelity: Remastered console route through BioShock: The Collection.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced exclusive content over the Windows remaster.

all_releases.fidelity: Mac remastered route.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced exclusive content over Windows Remastered.

all_releases.fidelity: Portable/console remastered route through BioShock: The Collection.
all_releases.reason: skip: portable convenience, not a fidelity or content win over Windows Remastered.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The Windows remaster is both the fidelity pick and the complete single-player route because the formerly PlayStation 3-exclusive Challenge Rooms are included in BioShock Remastered.

entries.remaster_caveats: Keep the original Windows release available as a fallback if the remaster's stability, audio behavior, or launcher flow interferes with capture.

entries.title: BioShock 2
entries.definitive_edition: BioShock 2 Remastered on Windows for single-player, original Windows for multiplayer only

emulation.notes: Use native Windows Remastered for single-player. Use original Windows only if multiplayer access is part of the archive target.

primary.why: BioShock 2 shipped on Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, and Mac OS X, with BioShock 2 Remastered later released through BioShock: The Collection. The Windows remaster is the best single-player route because it includes Minerva's Den and the remastered visual path, but it does not include the original multiplayer mode, so original Windows is preserved as a secondary route for that mode only.
primary.how_to_play: Use BioShock 2 Remastered on Windows for the campaign and Minerva's Den. If the multiplayer mode is part of the archive goal, install the original Windows version separately and treat multiplayer as secondary-only historical content.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original BioShock 2 multiplayer mode, absent from BioShock 2 Remastered.
secondary.what_to_play: Play or document only the multiplayer mode if functional access is available; do not replay the campaign.
secondary.why: The remastered version lacks the original multiplayer component.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PC release with campaign and multiplayer; lower visual route than the remaster.
all_releases.reason: secondary: use only for the original multiplayer mode missing from the remaster.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console release with multiplayer.
all_releases.reason: skip: original Windows covers the multiplayer secondary route with a better capture path.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console release with multiplayer.
all_releases.reason: skip: original Windows covers the multiplayer secondary route with a better capture path.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Mac route.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced exclusive content over the Windows original/remaster pairing.

all_releases.fidelity: Remastered PC route for campaign and Minerva's Den, with the strongest capture/settings ceiling.
all_releases.reason: primary: best-fidelity single-player route; pair with original Windows only for multiplayer.

all_releases.fidelity: Remastered console route through BioShock: The Collection.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced exclusive content over Windows Remastered, and it also lacks multiplayer.

all_releases.fidelity: Remastered console route through BioShock: The Collection.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced exclusive content over Windows Remastered, and it also lacks multiplayer.

all_releases.fidelity: Portable/console remastered route through BioShock: The Collection.
all_releases.reason: skip: portable convenience, but no sourced content win over Windows Remastered plus original-Windows multiplayer secondary.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: BioShock 2 Remastered is the fidelity pick for campaign and Minerva's Den, but the original multiplayer mode is absent from the remaster. Use Remastered for single-player and original Windows only for multiplayer documentation.

entries.remaster_caveats: BioShock 2 Remastered does not include the original multiplayer component. Do not treat the remaster as the complete all-modes version.

entries.title: BioShock Infinite
entries.definitive_edition: Windows with Season Pass / Complete Edition content

emulation.notes: Use native Windows. Console emulation is unnecessary for the researched route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native Windows with complete DLC installed

primary.version: BioShock Infinite with Season Pass / Complete Edition content
primary.why: BioShock Infinite released on PlayStation 3, Windows, Xbox 360, OS X, and Linux, then appeared on PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Nintendo Switch through BioShock: The Collection. The Complete Edition bundles the DLC, and the original PC version already met the graphical standard used for the updated console editions. Windows therefore remains the fidelity and complete-DLC route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Windows Steam build with the Season Pass/Complete Edition content installed, covering the campaign, Clash in the Clouds, and Burial at Sea. Keep launcher/Steam Deck notes current because 2K launcher behavior changed after earlier criticism.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console route.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower fidelity than Windows and no sourced exclusive content over the complete PC route.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PC route that already met the updated console graphical target, with full DLC/Season Pass path.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity and complete-DLC route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Windows is the fidelity route and supports the complete DLC package; no sourced platform-exclusive content is logged elsewhere.

entries.remaster_caveats: BioShock Infinite was not remastered for PC in the same way as the first two games because the PC version already met the collection's graphical target; keep current launcher behavior verified before capture.
